clue.text: Not ask enough when subject to an attack

definitions.meaning: to set too low a price on goods or services
read as two words, being under a charge, as troops are when charged by the enemy

explanation.surface: A seller asks too little while being pressured by an aggressive buyer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask too little money is a low billing; being beneath an assault is being 'under' a 'charge'.

clue.text: Experience travel by tube

parts.note: the Tube is London's Underground railway, so going by tube is going under
to travel is to go

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the experience of a ride on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground, which runs under the city.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to live through or suffer it, a synonym for experiencing it.

clue.text: County bowler

definitions.meaning: Derbyshire's county town, often standing for the county itself
a bowler hat is called a ... in American English

explanation.definitionFit: Derby is the county town of Derbyshire in England; a stiff round-crowned hat is known in the US by this name.

clue.text: Not confused with right information going round about a physicist

indicators.note: confused means the letters of not and the right abbreviation are jumbled up

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A muddled scientist rejects correct facts, which keep circulating about him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round about a' is only padding before the definition. Wilhelm Röntgen discovered X-rays; GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilhelm Röntgen was the German scientist who discovered X-rays in 1895.

clue.text: Great bravery, more his undoing

indicators.note: undoing suggests the letters of more his are taken apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A man's daring courage proves to be his downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undoing' rearranges the seven letters of MORE HIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroism is the quality of great courage, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Restrained journalists in a rush

indicators.note: in means the journalists' word is set inside the plant word

parts.note: a reed is a type of rush, a tall waterside plant
the press is the collective term for journalists

explanation.surface: Reporters in a hurry are held back from covering a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a rush' looks like haste, but it is the waterside plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Repressed means held back or kept under control, matching restrained.

clue.text: Omission of lions ie peculiar

indicators.note: peculiar suggests the letters of lions ie are strangely arranged

explanation.surface: An oddity: the big cats have been left out of the zoo guide.
explanation.definitionFit: Elision is the leaving out of a sound or syllable in speech, a kind of omission.

clue.text: Sorrowful even with a household implement

parts.note: sorrowful means sad
to even out creases is to iron them flat

explanation.surface: Someone is gloomy even when holding a domestic tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even' looks like an adverb, but it is the verb 'make smooth'. A sadiron is an old flatiron heated on a stove.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadiron is a heavy flatiron heated on the stove, an old domestic pressing tool.

clue.text: Hidden sign of office workers

parts.note: hidden means secret
Aries the ram is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A secret signal identifies the clerical staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' is a sign of the zodiac: ARIES, the ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Secretaries are clerical staff who handle correspondence and records in an office.

clue.text: Not a first impression

parts.note: an impression is also a print run of a book, so a later one is a second printing

explanation.definitionFit: A later printing of a book is called a second impression, so it is not the first.

clue.text: Platter chap has for a hearty eater

parts.note: a trencher is a wooden platter for serving food
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man with a big serving dish is clearly a big appetite.
explanation.walkthrough: A trencher is an old wooden platter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trencherman is someone with a big appetite, from the trencher once used to serve food.

clue.text: Dress for a meal

definitions.meaning: to dress or groom, as with leather or a horse's coat
a spiced dish of Indian origin

explanation.definitionFit: Currying leather means dressing it after tanning; a spiced stew is a dish served as dinner.

clue.text: Lead Neil over and give him an indication of the course to be followed

definitions.text: indication of the course to be followed

parts.note: to lead is to guide

indicators.note: over suggests the name Neil is turned about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shows Neil the way and gives him directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' rearranges NEIL into LINE; 'and give him an' is linking padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A guideline is a rule or principle pointing the way forward, an indication of what to do.

clue.text: Wearing down Rosie, no trouble

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters of Rosie and no are disturbed

explanation.surface: Rosie is worn out but insists there is no problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Erosion is the gradual wearing away of rock or soil by wind and water.

clue.text: Indiscreet saucy redhead was taken in

indicators.note: was taken in means the red's first letter is placed inside the saucy word

parts.note: saucy means impudent, cheeky
the head of the word red is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cheeky ginger-haired person was fooled by a careless remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redhead' is the first letter of 'red', R, which goes inside IMPUDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent means lacking care or good judgement, which is being unwise or rash.

clue.text: Graduate removing icons from the lodge

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

indicators.note: removing suggests the letters are moved about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A graduate takes the religious images away from the lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's idea is that taking ICONS out of the answer leaves MA; parsed forward, MA and ICONS are rearranged together, with 'removing' as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasons meet in lodges, so anything belonging to a Masonic lodge is described by this adjective.

clue.text: By the way a supporter's holding the ball

indicators.note: holding means the supporter's word wraps around the ball

parts.note: a prop is a supporter, and the possessive gives props
a ball is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Incidentally, a rugby prop forward is carrying the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter's' is read as a plural, with the ball going in before the final S. In rugby a prop is a forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos is used to introduce a remark incidentally, like 'by the way'.

clue.text: Deflect rays of light in a more fractured way

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words more fractured, straddling the two

explanation.surface: A physics lesson describes light bent in a more broken fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more fractured' sounds like the wordplay's meaning, but the answer simply runs across its words; 'in' points inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one medium into another.

clue.text: Dines out, that is to say, without a day appointed

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of dines are thrown out of order

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is to say

explanation.surface: Someone eats out with no date ever fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DINES into SINED. Sine die is Latin, used for an adjournment with no date to resume.
explanation.definitionFit: Sine die is Latin for adjourning indefinitely, with no date fixed to reconvene.

clue.text: Plead to change into a jumper at an early stage

indicators.note: to change suggests the letters of plead and to are reordered

explanation.surface: A plea that something should be turned into a sweater early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges PLEAD TO. 'jumper' looks like a sweater, but it is the frog.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the larval form of a frog, a leaping creature, before it grows legs.

clue.text: Support for the board

parts.note: board can be a table top as well as a company board of directors

explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a frame of legs supporting a table top or plank.

clue.text: Lost red revolutionary, one long in the tooth?

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests the letters of lost red are turned over and reordered

explanation.surface: A lost communist rebel has grown old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' rearranges LOST RED; 'red' hints at a communist, a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Long in the tooth is an idiom for being aged, from horses' gums receding with years.

clue.text: Bring pressure to bear on agency

definitions.meaning: a verb meaning to sway or affect
a noun meaning a force at work producing an effect

explanation.definitionFit: To sway someone is to apply pressure; an agency can be the power or effect by which something is done.

clue.text: Lady who is crazy the morning after

indicators.note: after places the morning abbreviation behind the crazy word

parts.note: crazy means mad
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, the morning

explanation.surface: A woman behaves wildly the next morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who is' is only a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is a polite term of address for a woman, a synonym of lady.

clue.text: Cast down

parts.note: cast means shed, and down is the soft feathers of a bird, not a gloomy mood

explanation.definitionFit: Birds shed their feathers seasonally, and to cast off soft plumage is to do exactly that.

clue.text: Is it not meant to grow in the water?

definitions.text: Is it not meant to grow in the water?

parts.words: Is it not meant to grow in the water?
parts.note: a weed is a plant growing where it is not wanted, and this one lives in the sea

explanation.definitionFit: Marine algae such as kelp are plants of the ocean, and the name suggests an unwanted plant.

clue.text: Where they never stop teasing in the West Country?

definitions.text: Where they never stop teasing in the West Country?

parts.words: Where they never stop teasing in the West Country?
parts.note: read as two words, a place where people keep on mocking, which is a Somerset town

explanation.definitionFit: Taunton is the county town of Somerset in south-west England; its name splits as taunt plus on.

clue.text: Strictly directed at landlord

parts.note: directed at means to, as in a letter sent to someone
a landlord lets property, so is the letter of it

explanation.surface: Correspondence addressed to the landlord follows exact instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landlord' is read as the one who lets property: the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Following instructions exactly, word for word, is doing them strictly.
